attributes.body:
The adverbial particle も is often used for labeling (A) as part of a category, when it would not usually be considered part of that group. In this way, it emphasizes that (A)'s inclusion is something that is surprising/unexpected in some way.

When も is used after a specific number + counter, it shows that the number itself is surprising. This can be when the actual number is lower, or higher than what was expected. Due to this, も can translate as 'as much as (A)', or 'not even (A)', and other similar phrases in this expression.

At first glance, this may seem different than も's translation as 'too' or 'also', but in those cases, も is also just pointing out that the something unexpected is part of whatever group was initially highlighted.

The above sentence just shows that the (B) speaker is unexpectedly putting themselves in the group that the (A) speaker initially only considered themselves to be a part of.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese
[DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: How to use the particle も

attributes.body: からする can be thought of as a more formal equivalent of もする when following number (or number+counter) expressions, e.g. 100万円からする時計 ('a watch that costs as much as 1,000,000 yen') vs. 100万円もする時計 (same meaning, but more colloquial).

first_relatable.title: からする
first_relatable.meaning: About, Or more, Over, Starts at

attributes.body: Number + も emphasizes a large quantity, like 'as many as (A)' or 'a whole (A)' in English. In contrast, Number + しか〜ない emphasizes a small quantity. For example, おにぎりを３個も食べた ('I ate three whole rice balls.') vs. おにぎり１個しか食べなかった ('I only ate one rice ball.').

second_relatable.title: Number + しか〜ない
second_relatable.meaning: No more than, Not exceeding, As few as・as little as, Only

attributes.body: Both forms emphasize quantity, but with contrasting nuance. Number/Amount + は implies 'at least' that amount, with a contrastive tone. For example, ３０分はかかると思うけど ('I think it'll take at least 30 minutes.', implying that it won't be less, but might be more.). In contrast, Number + も emphasizes the amount as if the speaker believes it is a lot, e.g., ３０分もかかった ('It took thirty whole minutes.').

first_relatable.title: Number/Amount + は
first_relatable.meaning: At least, Sort of, Or so

attributes.body: These patterns are similar in that both combine a counting expression with a particle. なん + counter + か combines the question word 何 (なん or なに) with a counter to mean 'a few (A)' or 'some amount of (A)', for example 何人か 'a few people.' In contrast, Number + も emphasizes that the number is large, e.g. １０００人も来た ('A whole 1000 people came.')
